speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how old you are and if you have experienced any periods yet? Also, have you had any broken bones in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of ambiguous genitalia at birth, severe acne, and bone fragility, I need to assess your physical development and hormone levels. Have you experienced any significant height growth in the last year, and do you have excessive hair growth on your face or body? REQUEST TEST: Karyotype; REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone; REQUEST TEST: Serum testosterone; REQUEST TEST: DEXA scan

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal 17-hydroxyprogesterone rules out classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, so we must look for other causes of virilization and bone loss. Are you experiencing excessive hair growth on your face or body, and have you noticed any changes in your voice or muscle mass? REQUEST TEST: Serum DHEA-S; REQUEST TEST: Serum LH; REQUEST TEST: Serum FSH

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal hormone levels make a functional androgen-secreting tumor or classic CAH unlikely, so I need to investigate structural causes for the virilization and bone fragility. Do you have a history of frequent infections, and do you exhibit any skeletal abnormalities such as short stature or bowing of the legs? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic Ultrasound; REQUEST TEST: Bone Marrow Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic Ultrasound: Ovaries with multiple cysts and a normal uterus. Bone Marrow Biopsy: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal bone marrow biopsy rules out leukemia or other marrow disorders, but the pelvic ultrasound showing ovarian cysts combined with virilization and bone fragility is highly suggestive of a metabolic or genetic condition. Let's evaluate your skeletal structure more closely; do you have a tall, slender build with long, thin fingers and toes, or have you ever been told you have a flexible joint? REQUEST TEST: Genetic testing for FBN1 gene; REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal FBN1 and echocardiogram results rule out Marfan syndrome, so I must consider other genetic causes for the combination of primary amenorrhea, virilization, and bone fragility. Do you have a history of easy bruising or abnormal bleeding, and have you ever been diagnosed with a bleeding disorder like von Willebrand disease? REQUEST TEST: Factor IX activity; REQUEST TEST: Androgen Receptor gene sequencing

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal androgen receptor sequencing rules out complete androgen insensitivity syndrome, which leaves us with a rare enzyme deficiency. Do you have elevated blood pressure or a history of low potassium levels, and have you noticed any muscle weakness? REQUEST TEST: Serum Aldosterone; REQUEST TEST: Serum Cortisol

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of ambiguous genitalia, severe acne, and bone fragility with normal classic CAH markers, I suspect a rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia such as 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxypregnenolone; REQUEST TEST: Serum DHEA-S

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum 17-hydroxypregnenolone: Elevated; Serum DHEA-S: Elevated

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated 17-hydroxypregnenolone and DHEA-S confirm a defect in 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, leading to androgen excess and virilization. DIAGNOSIS READY: 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency
